docs.t: Maximum takeoff and landing tailwind component?
docs.x: Maximum takeoff and landing tailwind component? 15 knots Maximum Takeoff and Landing Tailwind Component: 15 knots. FCTM 3.11 technique: a rolling takeoff is strongly advised when crosswinds exceed 20 knots or tailwinds exceed 5 knots (engine stress and possible surge if thrust is set before brake release). Airplane General

docs.t: Maximum runway slope?
docs.x: Maximum runway slope? +/- 2% Runway slope: +/- 2%. Airplane General

docs.t: Maximum operating altitude?
docs.x: Maximum operating altitude? 43,100 ft pressure altitude Maximum Operating Altitude: 43,100 ft pressure altitude. Airplane General

docs.t: Maximum takeoff and landing altitude?
docs.x: Maximum takeoff and landing altitude? 14,000 ft pressure altitude Maximum Takeoff and Landing Altitude: 14,000 ft pressure altitude. Airplane General

docs.t: Operating HF radios when refueling?
docs.x: Operating HF radios when refueling? Prohibited Do not operate HF radios when refueling. Airplane General

docs.t: Flying in RVSM airspace on ISFD alone?
docs.x: Flying in RVSM airspace on ISFD alone? Prohibited (standby altimeter does not meet RVSM accuracy) Do not fly in RVSM airspace on ISFD alone. The standby altimeter does not meet RVSM altimeter accuracy requirements. Airplane General

docs.t: Severe turbulent air penetration speed?
docs.x: Severe turbulent air penetration speed? 290 KIAS below 25,000 ft; 310 KIAS / .84 Mach (whichever lower) at and above 25,000 ft Severe turbulent air penetration speed (in severe turbulence) is defined as: 290 KIAS below 25,000 feet; 310 KIAS/.84 Mach (whichever is lower) at and above 25,000 feet. Airplane General

docs.t: Weather radar operation in a hangar?
docs.x: Weather radar operation in a hangar? Avoid (test mode exempt) Avoid weather radar operation in a hangar. Note: The hangar recommendation does not apply to the weather radar test mode. Airplane General

docs.t: Max allowable difference between Capt/FO altitude display and field elevation prior to takeoff?
docs.x: Max allowable difference between Capt/FO altitude display and field elevation prior to takeoff? 75 feet Prior to takeoff the maximum allowable difference between Captain's or First Officer's altitude display and field elevation is 75 feet. Airplane General

docs.t: Maximum demonstrated crosswind, takeoff and landing?
docs.x: Maximum demonstrated crosswind, takeoff and landing? 33 kt takeoff, 40 kt landing (gust included) - certification only, not operational limits The maximum demonstrated crosswind for takeoff is 33 knots (gust included), and the maximum demonstrated crosswind component for landing is 40 knots (gust included). Note: The demonstrated crosswinds are for certification only and do not represent operational limitations. Operational landing crosswind limitations, gusts included, are published in FCTM 6.29: dry 40 kt, wet 40 kt, standing water/slush 20 kt, snow (no melting) 35 kt, ice (no melting) 17 kt. Crosswind

docs.t: Sideslip-only (zero crab) landings are not recommended above what crosswind?
docs.x: Sideslip-only (zero crab) landings are not recommended above what crosswind? 25 knots Sideslip only (zero crab) landings are not recommended with crosswind components in excess of 25 knots. Crosswind

docs.t: When must you reduce takeoff crosswind guidelines by 5 knots (GE engines)?
docs.x: When must you reduce takeoff crosswind guidelines by 5 knots (GE engines)? If thrust is above 40% N1 at brake release for takeoff roll Reduce all takeoff crosswind guidelines by 5 knots if thrust is above 40% N1 (GE engines) at brake release for takeoff roll. Crosswind

docs.t: Reduce landing crosswind limit by 5 knots on wet/contaminated runways when?
docs.x: Reduce landing crosswind limit by 5 knots on wet/contaminated runways when? Whenever asymmetric reverse thrust is used Reduce crosswind limitation by 5 knots on wet or contaminated runways whenever asymmetric reverse thrust is used. Crosswind

docs.t: Maximum taxi weight?
docs.x: Maximum taxi weight? 563,000 lb Maximum Taxi Weight: 563,000 Pounds. Weights

docs.t: Maximum takeoff weight?
docs.x: Maximum takeoff weight? 561,500 lb Maximum Takeoff Weight: 561,500 Pounds. Weights

docs.t: Maximum landing weight?
docs.x: Maximum landing weight? 425,000 lb Maximum Landing Weight: 425,000 Pounds. Weights

docs.t: Maximum zero fuel weight?
docs.x: Maximum zero fuel weight? 400,000 lb Maximum Zero Fuel Weight: 400,000 Pounds. Weights

docs.t: Autopilot minimum engage altitude after takeoff?
docs.x: Autopilot minimum engage altitude after takeoff? 200 ft AGL The autopilot must not be engaged below a minimum engage altitude of 200 feet AGL after takeoff. Autoflight

docs.t: Autoland maximum airport field elevation?
docs.x: Autoland maximum airport field elevation? 8,400 ft Autoland capability may only be used for operations into runways at or below 8400 feet airport field elevation. Autoflight

docs.t: Without LAND 2 or LAND 3 annunciated, the autopilot must be disengaged below?
docs.x: Without LAND 2 or LAND 3 annunciated, the autopilot must be disengaged below? 135 ft AGL Without LAND 2 or LAND 3 annunciated, the autopilot must be disengaged below 135 feet AGL. Autoflight

docs.t: With LAND 2/3 and glideslope greater than 3.25 deg, the autopilot must be disengaged below?
docs.x: With LAND 2/3 and glideslope greater than 3.25 deg, the autopilot must be disengaged below? 100 ft AGL With LAND 2 or LAND 3 annunciated and glideslope angles greater than 3.25 degrees, the autopilot must be disengaged below 100 feet AGL. Autoflight

docs.t: If the glidepath angle is greater than 3.77 deg, the autopilot must be disengaged no later than?
docs.x: If the glidepath angle is greater than 3.77 deg, the autopilot must be disengaged no later than? 50 ft below DH/MDA If the glidepath angle for approach is greater than 3.77 degrees, the autopilot must be disengaged no later than 50 feet below DH/MDA. Autoflight

docs.t: Low weather minima takeoff guidance requirement?
docs.x: Low weather minima takeoff guidance requirement? ILS guidance only, on U.S. Type II or Type III ILS facilities Low weather minima takeoff may only be performed using ILS guidance on U.S. Type II or Type III ILS facilities. HUD Takeoff

docs.t: Maximum headwind (HUD takeoff and autoland)?
docs.x: Maximum headwind (HUD takeoff and autoland)? 25 knots HUD takeoff operations: Headwind 25 knots; Tailwind 15 knots; Crosswind 20 knots. Autoland operations: Headwind 25 knots; Tailwind 15 knots; Crosswind 25 knots (15 KTS for CAT II/III). HUD Takeoff / Autoland

docs.t: Maximum tailwind (HUD takeoff and autoland)?
docs.x: Maximum tailwind (HUD takeoff and autoland)? 15 knots HUD takeoff operations: Headwind 25 knots; Tailwind 15 knots; Crosswind 20 knots. Autoland operations: Headwind 25 knots; Tailwind 15 knots; Crosswind 25 knots (15 KTS for CAT II/III). HUD Takeoff / Autoland

docs.t: HUD takeoff: maximum crosswind?
docs.x: HUD takeoff: maximum crosswind? 20 knots Maximum wind component speeds when takeoff weather minima are predicated on HUD takeoff operations: Headwind 25 knots; Tailwind 15 knots; Crosswind 20 knots. HUD Takeoff

docs.t: Autoland: maximum crosswind?
docs.x: Autoland: maximum crosswind? 25 knots (15 knots for CAT II/III) Maximum wind component speeds when landing weather minima are predicated on autoland operations: Headwind 25 knots; Tailwind 15 knots; Crosswind 25 knots (15 KTS for CAT II/III). MEL note: autoland or LAND 3 may be inoperative for dispatch provided approach minimums do not require them (MEL 22-11-07A/B); with the aircraft downgraded to CAT I (MEL 05-10-01A), CAT II, CAT III, and autolands are not used. Autoland

docs.t: Autoland glideslope angle range?
docs.x: Autoland glideslope angle range? 2.5 to 3.25 degrees The maximum glideslope angle is 3.25 degrees. The minimum glideslope angle is 2.5 degrees. Autoland

docs.t: Autoland approved flap settings and engine config?
docs.x: Autoland approved flap settings and engine config? Flaps 20, 25, or 30; both engines operative or one engine inoperative Autoland capability may be used with flaps 20, 25, or 30, with both engines operative or with one engine inoperative. The AFDS autoland status annunciation must have LAND 2 or LAND 3 displayed. Autoland

docs.t: FLCH on final approach below what altitude?
docs.x: FLCH on final approach below what altitude? Do not use below 1,000 ft AFE Do not use FLCH on final approach below 1,000 feet AFE. Approach

docs.t: Using Capt/FO ACP to establish a SATCOM/cabin conference?
docs.x: Using Capt/FO ACP to establish a SATCOM/cabin conference? Prohibited Use of the captains or first officers ACP to establish a SATCOM/cabin conference is prohibited. Communications

docs.t: Takeoff and Go-Around thrust time limit?
docs.x: Takeoff and Go-Around thrust time limit? 5 minutes (10 minutes if one engine loses thrust) Takeoff and Go-Around Thrust Rating is limited to 5 minutes, or 10 minutes in the event of loss of thrust on one engine. Engines

docs.t: Minimum oil temperature for engine start?
docs.x: Minimum oil temperature for engine start? Greater than -40 deg C Oil temperature must be greater than -40 deg C for engine start. Engines

docs.t: Intentional selection of reverse thrust in flight?
docs.x: Intentional selection of reverse thrust in flight? Prohibited Intentional selection of reverse thrust in flight is prohibited. Engines

docs.t: Backing the airplane with reverse thrust?
docs.x: Backing the airplane with reverse thrust? Prohibited Backing the airplane with use of reverse thrust is prohibited. Engines

docs.t: Ground wind: thrust limit for winds greater than 55 knots?
docs.x: Ground wind: thrust limit for winds greater than 55 knots? Limit engine thrust to idle Ground wind operating envelope: for crosswinds greater than 40 knots, limit thrust to taxi (45% N1); with a tailwind greater than 5 knots and winds greater than 35 knots, limit to taxi (45% N1); for winds greater than 55 knots, limit engine thrust to idle. Engines

docs.t: Flight control mode required for takeoff?
docs.x: Flight control mode required for takeoff? Normal flight control mode only Takeoff is permitted only in the normal flight control mode. Flight Controls

docs.t: Rapid and large alternating control inputs?
docs.x: Rapid and large alternating control inputs? Avoid - structural failure risk at any speed, including below VA Avoid rapid and large alternating control inputs, especially in combination with large changes in pitch, roll, or yaw (e.g. large side slip angles) as they may result in structural failure at any speed, including below VA. Flight Controls

docs.t: Maximum altitude with flaps extended?
docs.x: Maximum altitude with flaps extended? 20,000 feet The maximum altitude with flaps extended is 20,000 feet. Flight Controls

docs.t: EFB portable keyboard and cable during takeoff and landing?
docs.x: EFB portable keyboard and cable during takeoff and landing? Must be stowed EFB portable keyboard and attaching cable (if installed) must be stowed during takeoff and landing. Flight Instruments

docs.t: Maximum tank fuel temperature at takeoff (Jet A / A-1 / JP-5 / JP-8 / TS-1)?
docs.x: Maximum tank fuel temperature at takeoff (Jet A / A-1 / JP-5 / JP-8 / TS-1)? 49 deg C (120 deg F) Maximum tank fuel temperature at takeoff is 49 deg C (120 deg F) for Jet A, Jet A-1, JP-5, JP-8 or TS-1. Fuel

docs.t: In-flight fuel temperature limit (Jet A / A-1 / JP-5 / JP-8)?
docs.x: In-flight fuel temperature limit (Jet A / A-1 / JP-5 / JP-8)? 65 deg C (150 deg F) Inflight fuel temperature is limited to 65 deg C (150 deg F) for Jet A, Jet A-1, JP-5 or JP-8. Fuel

docs.t: Minimum tank fuel temperature prior to takeoff?
docs.x: Minimum tank fuel temperature prior to takeoff? Not less than -29 deg C (-20 deg F) Tank fuel temperature prior to takeoff must not be less than -29 deg C (-20 deg F). MEL note: with one heat exchanger bypass valve inoperative (MEL 29-11-09), fuel temperature must be above -7 deg C before takeoff. Fuel

docs.t: Minimum in-flight tank fuel temperature?
docs.x: Minimum in-flight tank fuel temperature? At least -42 deg C, and at least 3 deg C above the freezing point of the fuel In-flight tank fuel temperature must be maintained at least -42 deg C, as well as 3 deg C above the freezing point of the fuel being used. Fuel

docs.t: Center tank fuel loading rule?
docs.x: Center tank fuel loading rule? Main tanks must be scheduled full if center tank fuel is loaded Main tanks must be scheduled to be full if center tank fuel is loaded. MEL note: with center tank override/jettison pumps deferred (MEL 28-22-02), center tank fuel must be accounted for in weight and balance in case it cannot be used, and main tank fuel must be adequate to reach a suitable airport if the scavenge system fails. Fuel

docs.t: Using the terrain display for navigation?
docs.x: Using the terrain display for navigation? Do not use the terrain display for navigation Do not use the terrain display for navigation. Warning Systems
